response: {"title":"Reject-before-mutation invariant","intervention":"For every edited path that can reject an input, verify on one representative invalid boundary that the exact exception class and message occur before any mutation of arguments, object state, files, caches, or collaborators.","claim":"Against no appended instruction, this reject-before-mutation invariant will improve held-out invalid-input correctness on matched Python tasks under an identical deadline, while wall_time and turns measure overhead.","mechanism":"Checking both the exact error and the pre-error state catches partial side effects caused by late validation, a failure invisible when tests assert only that an exception was raised.","assumptions":["Invalid-input behavior is intended to be atomic for affected APIs.","Relevant mutable state can be observed or snapshotted cheaply.","A representative invalid boundary exercises each edited rejection path."],"risks":["Some APIs intentionally mutate state before reporting an error.","Hidden external side effects may not be observable in a local snapshot.","Snapshot setup can consume deadline time or introduce brittle tests.","One representative invalid value may miss mutations on other rejection branches."],"test_plan":{"experiment":"Randomly assign matched multi-module Python repairs to this appended instruction or no appended instruction under identical model, tools, and deadline; evaluate hidden invalid-input cases for exact errors and state atomicity, plus boundary pass rate.","metrics":["pass_rate","wall_time","turns"],"success_condition":"The intervention arm has higher hidden pass_rate on invalid-input atomicity and overall edge semantics, stays within the deadline, and does not materially increase median turns."},"single_shot_ordinal":8}
